Conclusion: the integration must expect an `InvalidCursorError` (an `OrdariumError` subclass) with `code === "INVALID_CURSOR"` and the message "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point". It is a fail-closed caller-input failure, not ledger damage, and there is no numeric error code to branch on.

What the "observation cursor" is: in the pinned Ordarium contract, `StateChangePage.cursor` is documented as the "opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" for "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0)" (`node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts`, `state.d.ts` `StateChangeFeed.changes(filter?, cursor?)`). A consumer persists that cursor and re-supplies it; that is the "stored observation cursor".

Rejection path in the exact pinned version (verified 1.3.1 in package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, and node_modules/@ordarium/{core,ledger-sqlite}/package.json — all three agree):
- `@ordarium/core/dist/src/errors.d.ts|js`: `InvalidCursorError` → code `"INVALID_CURSOR"`, documented as "a caller-supplied change-feed cursor could not be decoded as a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0); distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT … it fails closed instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed."
- `@ordarium/core/dist/src/ledger.js` (`decodeStateChangeCursor`) and `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` `changes()` both throw it for a malformed/undecodable cursor, and also when the stored position exceeds the ledger high-water mark (e.g. cursor restored from a replaced/reset ledger — "ORD-BOOT-0.1").
- `InvalidCursorError` is re-exported from `@ordarium/core`, so the integration can classify it by `instanceof` (consistent with the alignment charter's rule to map errors by type, not numeric code).

Why not the alternative: the only contrary source is `docs/engineering/notes/error-code-note.md`, which claims the failure "was surfaced as numeric code 27". That file self-declares "Status: informational, not normative", and it is also factually off: `docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md` §1.2/§2 item 3 assigns codes 27–29 to `STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT`/`STATE_REF_NOT_FOUND` (state CAS/refs), not to cursor rejection. Under `docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md`, (1) the published contract of the exact pinned version governs the dependency interface, and (3) informational/historical records never override it. The exact pinned version is 1.3.1, and its shipped declarations define `INVALID_CURSOR`. The 1.2.0 references in the alignment charter are dated historical entries, not a competing interface authority.

Related-but-different failures that should NOT be confused with this one: `LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` is thrown when the ledger does not declare `stateChangeFeed` at all (capability gate, before any cursor is consulted); `LedgerCorruptError` (`LEDGER_CORRUPT`) is for dangling/damaged ledger content; and the plain list-pagination path (`store.list(..., nextCursor)`) rejects a bad cursor with a bare `TypeError("Opaque state list cursor is invalid")`, which is a different surface from the observation/change-feed cursor.

Resolved locally without peer contact: the load-bearing conflict (note vs. pinned shipped contract) is settled by the repo's own normative source-precedence rule plus the readable exact-version contract; no missing resolution owned by the Ordarium peer.
